:::{#exm-ppv-sens-spec-prev}
#### PPV of a COVID-19 test, from the two ratios

For the COVID-19 test of @exm-sensitivity and @exm-specificity,
used in the population of @exm-prevalence,
@thm-ppv-sens-spec-prev gives:

$$
\ba
\text{PPV}
&= \frac{1}{1 + \frac{1 - 0.99}{0.99} \cd \frac{1 - 0.07}{0.07}}
&& \text{(PPV in terms of the two ratios, with the given values)} \\
&= \frac{1}{1 + \frac{0.01}{0.99} \cd \frac{0.93}{0.07}}
&& \text{(subtract in each numerator)} \\
&\approx \frac{1}{1 + 0.0101 \cd 13.29}
&& \text{(divide in each ratio)} \\
&\approx \frac{1}{1 + 0.134}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= \frac{1}{1.134}
&& \text{(add)} \\
&\approx 0.88
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

This value matches @exm-ppv.

If the same test were used in a population with prevalence 0.1% instead,
the ratio of non-diseased to diseased people would be $0.999 / 0.001 = 999$,
and the PPV would fall to

$$
\ba
\text{PPV}
&= \frac{1}{1 + \frac{0.01}{0.99} \cd 999}
&& \text{(PPV in terms of the two ratios, with the new prevalence)} \\
&\approx \frac{1}{1 + 0.0101 \cd 999}
&& \text{(divide)} \\
&\approx \frac{1}{1 + 10.09}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= \frac{1}{11.09}
&& \text{(add)} \\
&\approx 0.09
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

so about 9 in 10 positive results would be false positives.

:::
